brief: 5 SaaS categories AI agents are killing in 2026 — and what to build instead.

slots.title: 1. Support desks, the target
slots.body: Ticket-based helpdesks die as autonomous agents resolve refunds, track orders, and talk to customers without playbooks.

slots.title: 2. Zapier-style automation, dead
slots.body: Static if-this-then-that workflows collapse when agents negotiate APIs, handle errors, and rewrite their own logic on the fly.

slots.title: 3. Content farms, obsolete
slots.body: Template-based blog and social tools lose to agents that research niches, draft threads, and post across channels without human review.

slots.title: 4. Code snippets, retired
slots.body: Copilots that suggest single lines are replaced by agents that refactor repos, write tests, and ship features end to end.

slots.title: 5. Meeting notetakers, buried
slots.body: Transcription apps become irrelevant when agents attend calls, extract tasks, update CRMs, and schedule follow-ups while you sleep.

slots.title: 6. Agent infra, the play
slots.body: Don't build another wrapper. Build memory layers, evaluation frameworks, and permission systems that let agents run businesses, not tasks.
